---
title: "SNCSTM simulation: SI and IV"
output: html_document
---

This pipeline generates one dataset under sequential ignorability (SI) and one
under instrumental-variable (IV) identification, then estimates both causes.
`n` is the number of individuals per dataset; `seed` identifies one simulation
replication. The optional Monte Carlo section at the end is disabled by default.

## Settings and functions

Run the chunks in order from the project root, or render this document.
Supported event-rate settings are 0.07, 0.15, 0.30, and 0.60.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)
stopifnot(requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE))

n <- 10000
seed <- 1
event_rate <- 0.30

source("R/SI.R")
source("R/IV.R")
```

## SI: generate data

```{r si-generation}
si_simulation <- simulation_si(n = n, seed = seed, event_rate = event_rate)
si_data <- si_simulation$observed
head(si_data)
```

## SI: fit nuisance models and estimate both causes

Treatment and censoring nuisance models are fitted once and shared by both causes.

```{r si-estimation}
si_nuisance <- fit_si_nuisance(si_data)
si_fits <- lapply(1:2, function(cause) {
  estimation_si(si_data, cause = cause, n_grid = 10, nuisance = si_nuisance)
})
```

### Four targets for each cause

Report cumulative effects at the left limits of 0.5, 1, and 1.5, and the pooled
beta, with analytical standard errors and pointwise 95% confidence intervals.
Only the display combines `B_summary` and `pooled`; the estimator is unchanged.

```{r si-results}
si_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(si_fits, function(fit) {
  B <- fit$B_summary
  pooled <- fit$pooled
  data.frame(
    cause = pooled$cause,
    parameter = c(paste0("B(", B$time, ")"), "beta (pooled)"),
    estimate = c(B$B, pooled$beta),
    std = c(B$std_B, pooled$std),
    lower = c(B$lower, pooled$beta - 1.96 * pooled$std),
    upper = c(B$upper, pooled$beta + 1.96 * pooled$std),
    truth = si_simulation$parameters$beta[pooled$cause] * c(B$time, 1)
  )
}))
si_results
```

## IV: generate data

```{r iv-generation}
iv_simulation <- simulation_iv(n = n, seed = seed, event_rate = event_rate)
iv_data <- iv_simulation$observed
head(iv_data)
```

## IV: fit nuisance models and estimate both causes

Instrument-mean and censoring nuisance models are fitted once and shared by both causes.

```{r iv-estimation}
iv_nuisance <- fit_iv_nuisance(iv_data)
iv_fits <- lapply(1:2, function(cause) {
  estimation_iv(iv_data, cause = cause, n_grid = 10, nuisance = iv_nuisance)
})
```

### Four targets for each cause

Each cause has three cumulative-effect estimates and one pooled estimate, with
analytical standard errors and pointwise 95% confidence intervals.

```{r iv-results}
iv_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(iv_fits, function(fit) fit$summary))
iv_results$truth <- iv_simulation$parameters$beta[iv_results$cause] * rep(c(.5, 1, 1.5, 1), 2)
iv_results <- iv_results[c("cause", "parameter", "estimate", "std", "lower", "upper", "truth")]
iv_results
```

## Monte Carlo simulation (disabled by default)

All chunks below use `eval=FALSE`, so rendering this document runs only the
single-seed examples above. To run Monte Carlo simulations, execute these chunks
manually in order from the project root. The existing runners preserve the data
generators, nuisance fits, estimators, analytical SEs, and `n_grid = 10`.

### Settings

The number of replications is controlled by `B`: use `B = 5` for a small test
or `B = 1000` for the original simulations. Each method uses seeds 1 through `B`;
the single-run `seed` above does not change this sequence. Each seed generates a new
dataset and estimates both causes. The Monte Carlo section uses all three sample
sizes from the manuscript table and the event rate above (0.30). The single-run
section still uses `n = 10000`. Set `sample_sizes <- n` for that size alone.

```{r mc-settings, eval=FALSE}
B <- 5
# B <- 1000
sample_sizes <- c(1000, 5000, 10000)
stopifnot(length(B) == 1, B %in% 1:1000,
          all(sample_sizes %in% c(1000, 5000, 10000)),
          !anyDuplicated(sample_sizes), event_rate %in% c(.07, .15, .30, .60))
seeds <- seq_len(B)
rate_tag <- sprintf("%02d", round(100 * event_rate))
jobs <- expand.grid(method = c("si_cumulative", "iv_table1"), n = sample_sizes,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
jobs$output <- sprintf("results/results_%s_%s_n%d", jobs$method, rate_tag, jobs$n)
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
```

### Run individual replications

Run sequentially, with one fresh R process per seed. Each runner saves eight
target rows and its code fingerprints. Existing files with different settings
or code cause an error; matching files are recomputed if this chunk is rerun.

```{r mc-run, eval=FALSE}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(jobs))) {
  job <- jobs[i, ]
  for (id in seeds) {
    cat(job$method, "n =", job$n, "seed =", id, "\n")
    status <- system2(rscript, shQuote(c(
      paste0("scripts/run_", job$method, ".R"), id, job$n, job$output, event_rate
    )), stdout = FALSE)
    if (status != 0) stop("Run failed: ", job$method, ", n=", job$n, ", seed=", id)
  }
}
```

### Merge saved replications

The original merge scripts read seeds 1 through `B` and recompute summaries
from individual estimates. They do not generate data or fit models. As in the
original scripts, failed estimates are recorded and finite results are used;
inspect the success counts below before interpreting the table.

```{r mc-merge, eval=FALSE}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(jobs))) {
  job <- jobs[i, ]
  status <- system2(rscript, shQuote(c(
    paste0("scripts/merge_", job$method, ".R"), job$output, B
  )))
  if (status != 0) stop("Merge failed: ", job$method, ", n=", job$n)
}
```

### SI and IV comparison table

Percent bias is `100 * abs(Bias / truth)`. The original summaries call MCSD
`SEE` and average estimated SE `SD`; coverage `CP` is already in percent.
Only display labels and formatting change here. Estimates and summaries retain
the original precision in the saved RDS files.

```{r mc-table, eval=FALSE}
mc_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
  job <- jobs[i, ]
  file <- file.path(job$output, sprintf("%s_%s_n%d.rds", job$method, rate_tag, job$n))
  x <- readRDS(file)$summary
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 8, all(x$n == job$n), all(x$event_rate == event_rate),
            all(x$simulations == B))
  x$method <- if (job$method == "si_cumulative") "SI" else "IV"
  x$parameter <- sub("B_D(", "B(", x$parameter, fixed = TRUE)
  x[c("method", "n", "cause", "parameter", "truth", "simulations",
      "successful_estimates", "successful_intervals", "Bias", "SEE", "SD", "CP")]
}))
mc_summary[c("method", "n", "cause", "parameter", "simulations",
             "successful_estimates", "successful_intervals")]

targets <- c("B(0.5)", "B(1)", "B(1.5)", "beta (pooled)")
mc_tables <- list()
for (sample_size in sample_sizes) for (cause in 1:2) {
  sides <- lapply(c("SI", "IV"), function(method) {
    x <- mc_summary[mc_summary$method == method & mc_summary$n == sample_size &
                      mc_summary$cause == cause, ]
    stopifnot(nrow(x) == 4, setequal(x$parameter, targets))
    x <- x[match(targets, x$parameter), ]
    values <- rbind(sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * abs(x$Bias / x$truth)),
                    sprintf("%.3f", x$SEE), sprintf("%.3f", x$SD),
                    sprintf("%.1f%%", x$CP))
    colnames(values) <- paste(method, targets)
    values
  })
  mc_tables[[length(mc_tables) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    n = sample_size, cause = cause,
    Metric = c("Perc. Bias", "MCSD", "Ave. SE", "95% CP"),
    sides[[1]], sides[[2]], check.names = FALSE
  )
}
mc_table <- do.call(rbind, mc_tables)
knitr::kable(mc_table, row.names = FALSE)
```
